days.title: Day 1
days.body:
Devotion
Peace doesn't begin when everything around you is finally in order. It begins when your heart finds its place in God.

We often think that if we could fix a particular problem, receive a particular answer, achieve a certain goal, or get clarity about our future, then we would finally have peace. But God invites us to experience peace even before those things happen.

The peace of God is not dependent on your circumstances becoming perfect. It comes from knowing that your life is held by a perfect God.

When your mind is fixed on your problems, your problems become bigger. When your mind is fixed on God, you begin to remember who is bigger than your problems.

Today, don't try to figure everything out. Come before God, slow down, and allow your heart to rest in Him.

Reflect:
- What has been occupying my mind more than God lately?
- Am I trusting God, or am I trying to control everything myself?
Prayer:

Lord, bring my heart back to You. Teach me to trust You even when I don't understand what is happening around me. Help me to stop carrying things that I have already placed in Your hands. Fix my mind upon You, and let Your presence become the place where my heart finds rest. Amen.

days.title: Day 2
days.body:
Devotion
Jesus never promised that we would have a life without trouble. But He promised us something greater than the absence of trouble — His presence in the middle of it.

The world offers peace when everything is going well. When finances are stable, relationships are good, plans are working, and the future looks certain. But the peace Jesus gives is different. His peace can remain even when life is uncertain.

You don't have to carry tomorrow today. You don't have to have every answer before you can rest. You don't have to pretend you're strong when you feel tired.

Jesus knows what troubles your heart. He knows the things you haven't told anyone. And He invites you to trust Him.

Let today be a reminder that peace is not something you have to manufacture. It is something you receive from Christ.

Reflect:
- What am I carrying today that Jesus is asking me to surrender?
- Am I looking for peace in circumstances, or in Christ?
Prayer:

Lord Jesus, thank You for the peace You give, a peace that the world cannot offer. I surrender my worries, my uncertainties, my fears, and the things I cannot control. Teach me to rest in Your promises and not be troubled by what I cannot see. Amen.

days.title: Day 3
days.body:
Devotion
Sometimes the reason we struggle to experience peace is because we never stop.

We are always thinking, planning, worrying, scrolling, working, expecting, or trying to solve something. Even when our bodies are resting, our minds are running.

But God says, Be still.

Stillness is not giving up. Stillness is not laziness. Stillness is an act of faith. It is the moment you stop trying to be in control of everything and acknowledge that God is God, and you are not.

You may not know what tomorrow holds. You may not know how a situation will turn out. But you can know the One who holds tomorrow.

Today, make space for silence. Read the Word slowly. Don't rush through the chapters just to finish them. Sit with a verse. Let God speak before you speak, and let His presence settle your heart.

Reflect:
- When was the last time I was genuinely still before God?
- What would it look like for me to trust God without constantly trying to figure everything out?
Prayer:

Father, quiet my mind. Help me to stop being consumed by the things around me. Teach me the beauty of being still in Your presence. When my thoughts become loud, remind me that You are God, You are in control, and You are faithful. Amen.

days.title: Day 4
days.body:
Devotion
Sometimes our lack of peace comes from fear — fear of losing something, fear of failing, fear of the unknown, fear that things will not work out, or even fear that God is somehow distant from us.

But Romans 8 reminds us of a truth that we must never forget: we are loved by God, and nothing can separate us from that love in Christ.

You may go through difficult seasons. You may have days when you don't feel spiritually strong. You may not always understand what God is doing. But His love is not changing according to your feelings, your circumstances, or your performance.

You don't have to earn God's love today. You don't have to prove yourself to Him. You can come to Him as you are.

When you know you are secure in God's love, you don't have to live in constant fear. You can face the unknown with confidence, not because you know what will happen, but because you know who holds you.

Reflect:
- Do I believe God's love for me remains even when I feel weak?
- What fear do I need to bring before Him today?
Prayer:

Father, thank You that Your love for me is not dependent on my strength or circumstances. Help me to live with the assurance that I belong to You. When fear comes, remind me of Your Word. Give me confidence to walk forward knowing that nothing can separate me from Your love. Amen.

days.title: Day 5
days.body:
Devotion
There is a difference between carrying something and surrendering something.

You can pray about a situation and still continue carrying it in your mind. You can say that you trust God, yet spend every day worrying about how things will turn out. Surrender means bringing it before God and trusting Him even when you don't have the ability to change the outcome.

God doesn't ask you to carry every burden by yourself. He invites you to bring it to Him because He cares for you.

Not just the big things. The little things too. Your disappointments, your unanswered prayers, your future, your family, your responsibilities, your thoughts, and the things that quietly trouble you.

As you conclude these five days, don't just leave with a feeling of peace. Leave with a decision to trust God daily.

Peace is not a one-time experience. It is a daily surrender.

Reflect:
- What am I still holding on to that I need to surrender to God?
- Can I trust God even if He doesn't answer in the way or timing I expect?
Prayer:

Father, I bring everything before You. Every burden, every concern, every fear, every unanswered question. I surrender what I cannot control and trust You with what I cannot understand. Thank You for caring for me. Help me to walk in Your peace, not only today, but every day. Let my heart rest in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.

title: Be Still

days.title: DAY 01 — BE STILL AND KNOW THAT HE IS GOD
days.body:
Theme: Learning to quiet our hearts in God's presence.

Key Scripture: Psalm 46:10
Devotion
There are moments in life when everything seems to be happening at once. Problems arise, responsibilities increase, and situations unfold that are beyond our control. In those moments, our natural response is often to worry, overthink, and try to find solutions through our own strength.

But Psalm 46:10 gives us a different instruction: "Be still, and know that I am God."

Notice that God does not say, "Fix everything and then come to Me." He does not say, "Understand everything before you trust Me." He simply tells us to be still and recognise who He is.

Stillness begins when we stop allowing our circumstances to become greater than our understanding of God.

Being still does not mean that we stop taking responsibility or making decisions. It means that we stop living as though everything depends entirely on us.

God is still God when life is uncertain. He is still God when prayers seem unanswered. He is still God when the future is unclear.

Today, take some time to put aside your worries, silence the distractions, and simply be in His presence. You do not always need to have something to say. Sometimes, the greatest expression of faith is simply resting in the knowledge of who God is.
Reflection
- What is currently making it difficult for me to experience stillness?
- Have I been trying to control things that I should surrender to God?
- When was the last time I spent time with God without distractions or expectations?
Prayer
Heavenly Father, teach me to be still in Your presence. Forgive me for the times I have allowed my worries, responsibilities, and circumstances to take control of my heart. Help me to recognise that You are sovereign over everything. Quiet my thoughts, settle my heart, and teach me to trust You even when I do not understand what is happening. May my life become a reflection of a heart that rests in You. In Jesus' name, Amen.

days.title: DAY 02 — THE POWER OF BEING STILL BEFORE GOD
days.body:
Theme: Finding strength through surrender rather than striving.

Key Scripture: Isaiah 30:15
Devotion
We live in a world that celebrates constant activity. We are encouraged to work harder, move faster, achieve more, and never stop. Sometimes, without even realising it, we bring that same mindset into our relationship with God.

We become so occupied with doing things for Him that we forget the importance of simply being with Him.

In Isaiah 30:15, God reminds His people that their strength would be found in returning, resting, quietness, and trust.

This is a powerful reminder that spiritual strength does not always come from doing more. Sometimes it comes from surrendering more.

Think about how often you try to solve everything yourself before turning to God. How often do you exhaust your own strength before seeking His direction?

God is not asking you to carry everything alone.

There is a difference between being busy and being fruitful. There is a difference between working in your own strength and walking in dependence on God.

Jesus Himself regularly withdrew from the crowds to spend time in prayer. If the Son of God made time to be alone with the Father, how much more should we recognise our need for that time?

Today, remember that stillness is not wasted time. It is a place where your heart is restored, your perspective is renewed, and your dependence on God grows.
Reflection
- Am I so occupied with doing things that I have neglected spending time with God?
- Do I depend more on my own strength or on God's strength?
- What distractions do I need to remove to create more room for God?
Prayer
Father, help me understand the importance of resting in Your presence. I do not want to become so busy with the things of this world that I forget the One who gives me life. Teach me to depend on Your strength rather than my own. Help me to slow down, surrender my ambitions, and seek You above everything else. Restore my soul and renew my heart. In Jesus' name, Amen.

days.title: DAY 03 — WHEN GOD SEEMS SILENT
days.body:
Theme: Trusting God even when we cannot hear or understand Him.

Key Scripture: 1 Kings 19:11–13
Devotion
One of the most difficult experiences in our walk with God is going through a season when He seems silent.

You pray, but the answer does not come. You seek direction, but the way forward remains unclear. You wait, but nothing seems to change.

In 1 Kings 19, we read about Elijah, who was experiencing a deeply difficult moment. God instructed him to stand on the mountain because the Lord was going to pass by.

A powerful wind came, followed by an earthquake and a fire. Yet the Lord was not revealed to Elijah through those dramatic events. Afterward came a gentle whisper.

Elijah had to become attentive enough to recognise that whisper.

Sometimes, we expect God to speak through extraordinary circumstances, dramatic signs, or immediate answers. But Scripture reminds us that we must also learn to listen quietly.

The noise around us can make it difficult to recognise what God is doing within us.

God's silence should never automatically be interpreted as God's absence. We may not understand His timing, but we can continue to trust His character.

There will be seasons when you will not have all the answers. Seasons when you must keep walking by faith rather than by sight.

Do not allow the absence of an immediate answer to make you abandon your relationship with God.

Today, create space to listen. Read His Word, pray, and remain attentive. You do not need to manufacture a voice from God. You need to remain grounded in what He has already revealed through Scripture.
Reflection
- How do I respond when God does not answer my prayers immediately?
- Have I become too distracted to recognise His guidance through His Word?
- Can I remain faithful even when I do not have all the answers?
Prayer
Lord, teach me to recognise Your presence even in seasons of silence. When I cannot understand what You are doing, help me to trust who You are. Quiet the noise within my heart and help me become attentive to Your Word. Give me patience to wait and faith to keep walking even when I cannot see what lies ahead. In Jesus' name, Amen.

days.title: DAY 04 — BE STILL IN THE MIDDLE OF THE STORM
days.body:
Theme: Finding peace in Jesus regardless of life's circumstances.

Key Scripture: Mark 4:35–41
Devotion
Sometimes, stillness is easy when everything is going well. When there are no problems, no unexpected challenges, and no difficult situations, it is easier to say that we trust God.

But what happens when the storm arrives?

In Mark 4, Jesus and His disciples were crossing the sea when a violent storm arose. The waves were breaking into the boat, and the disciples became terrified.

Yet Jesus was sleeping.

The disciples woke Him and asked whether He cared that they were perishing. Jesus arose, rebuked the wind, and commanded the sea to be still.

What a powerful picture of the difference between fear and faith.

The disciples were looking at the storm. Jesus was never overwhelmed by it.

We often find ourselves behaving like the disciples. When circumstances become difficult, we begin to question whether God sees us, whether He cares, and whether He is still in control.

But the presence of a storm does not mean the absence of Jesus.

Faith does not mean that storms will never come. It means that we have someone greater than the storm walking with us.

There are situations you cannot control. There are people you cannot change. There are outcomes you cannot predict.

But you can choose where to place your trust.

Today, do not allow the storm around you to become louder than the truth of God's presence in your life.
Reflection
- What storm am I currently facing?
- Have I allowed fear to become greater than my faith?
- How can I demonstrate trust in Jesus during my present circumstances?
Prayer
Lord Jesus, when the storms of life arise, remind me that You are with me. Forgive me for allowing fear to take control of my heart. Help me to trust You when circumstances are difficult and when I cannot see a way forward. Give me peace that does not depend on everything going according to my plans. Teach me to place my confidence in You alone. Amen.

days.title: DAY 05 — WAIT UPON THE LORD
days.body:
Theme: Learning patience and trusting God's timing.

Key Scripture: Isaiah 40:31
Devotion
Waiting is not something most of us enjoy.

We want answers quickly. We want prayers answered immediately. We want doors to open when we are ready, and we want to understand what God is doing in every season.

But God's timing does not always align with our expectations.

Isaiah 40:31 reminds us that those who wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength.

Waiting upon God is not passive resignation. It is an active expression of trust.

It means continuing to believe when the answer has not arrived. It means remaining obedient when the destination is unclear. It means refusing to run ahead of God simply because we are impatient.

Consider Abraham, who received a promise from God but had to wait. Consider Joseph, who went through years of difficulty before seeing the fulfilment of what God had shown him.

Their stories remind us that waiting can be part of our journey of faith.

Sometimes, God changes our circumstances. Sometimes, He changes us while we are waiting for our circumstances to change.

Do not mistake a waiting season for a wasted season.

Use this time to grow in faith, deepen your relationship with God, and become more grounded in His Word.

You do not need to force doors open that God has not opened. Learn to trust Him with the timing.
Reflection
- What am I currently waiting for God to do?
- Am I becoming impatient and trying to force things to happen?
- What can God teach me during this season of waiting?
Prayer
Heavenly Father, give me the patience to wait upon You. Help me not to run ahead of Your plans or become discouraged when things take longer than I expected. Renew my strength when I feel tired. Teach me to trust Your timing and remain faithful in every season. May I learn to value Your presence more than the answers I am waiting for. In Jesus' name, Amen.

days.title: DAY 06 — COME AWAY AND REST
days.body:
Theme: Making room for God through intentional solitude.

Key Scripture: Mark 6:31
Devotion
Jesus understood the importance of withdrawing from the demands of everyday life.

Throughout His ministry, people constantly surrounded Him. They needed healing, teaching, guidance, and miracles. Yet Jesus regularly made time to withdraw and pray.

In Mark 6:31, Jesus invited His disciples to come away to a quiet place and rest for a while.

This invitation reveals something important about our relationship with God: we were never meant to live in a constant state of exhaustion.

Sometimes, we become so consumed by our work, ministry, relationships, responsibilities, and even our service to others that we neglect our own spiritual well-being.

We may attend church, serve in ministry, help people, and participate in Christian activities, but still fail to spend meaningful time alone with God.

There is a difference between knowing about God and intentionally spending time with Him.

Stillness requires us to make room.

It may mean putting your phone away, stepping away from social media, finding a quiet place, opening your Bible, and spending time in prayer without rushing.

You do not need a perfect environment. You need a willing heart.

Today, accept the invitation to come away and rest. Let your relationship with God become more than a routine. Let it become the foundation of your everyday life.
Reflection
- Have I been making intentional time to be alone with God?
- What activities or distractions are taking too much of my attention?
- Is my relationship with God becoming a routine rather than a genuine relationship?
Prayer
Father, thank You for inviting me into Your presence. Forgive me for the times I have allowed busyness and distractions to take priority over spending time with You. Help me establish a deeper and more consistent relationship with You. Teach me to make room for stillness, prayer, and Your Word. May my desire for Your presence become greater than my desire for the things of this world. In Jesus' name, Amen.

days.title: DAY 07 — A LIFESTYLE OF STILLNESS
days.body:
Theme: Living every day with a heart surrendered to God.

Key Scripture: Psalm 131:1–2
Devotion
Over the past six days, we have explored what it means to be still before God. We have learned to quiet our hearts, surrender our worries, listen for His guidance, trust Him during storms, wait upon His timing, and make room for His presence.

But stillness should not be something we practise for only seven days.

It should become a lifestyle.

In Psalm 131, David describes his soul as being quieted and calmed, like a weaned child resting with its mother.

What a beautiful picture of spiritual maturity.

A child who is resting does not need to understand everything happening around them. They simply find comfort in the presence of the one caring for them.

In the same way, our relationship with God should grow beyond constantly seeking answers, solutions, and blessings. We should learn to delight in Him simply because He is God.

The world will continue to be noisy. Responsibilities will remain. Unexpected challenges will come. There will be days when your mind feels overwhelmed and your heart struggles to find peace.

But you can return to the presence of God.

You can begin each morning with prayer. You can meditate on His Word throughout the day. You can pause when anxiety begins to rise. You can surrender your plans before making decisions.

Remember, stillness is not about escaping life. It is about learning to live life with God at the centre.

As you complete these seven days, make a commitment to protect your time with God. Do not allow the busyness of life to take away the most important relationship you have.

Let your heart remain still in Him.
Reflection
- What have I learned about stillness during these seven days?
- What changes do I need to make to maintain a consistent relationship with God?
- How can I make stillness a daily part of my walk with Christ?
Prayer
Heavenly Father, thank You for walking with me through these seven days. I pray that the lessons I have learned will become part of my everyday life. Help me to seek You before anything else, trust You in every circumstance, and remain close to You in every season. When the world becomes noisy, remind me to return to Your presence. May my heart always find its rest in You. Let my life be led by Your Spirit and grounded in Your Word. In Jesus' name, Amen.

description: Theme Scripture: Psalm 46:10  “Be still, and know that I am God.” Introduction In a world that constantly demands our attention, stillness has become something we rarely experience. We wake up thinking about our responsibilities, spend our days chasing deadlines, and go to sleep with our minds occupied by tomorrow's worries.  But God invites us into something different.  Stillness is not simply the absence of noise. It is the decision to quiet our hearts before God, surrender our worries, trust His sovereignty, and recognise that He is in control even when life feels uncertain.  Throughout Scripture, we see that God often calls His people to be still, wait patiently, listen carefully, and trust Him completely. Moses stood before the Red Sea and was told to stand firm. David learned to rest in God's presence. Elijah discovered that God's voice was not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a gentle whisper. Jesus Himself withdrew from the crowds to spend time alone with the Father.  This seven-day devotional is an invitation to step away from the noise of the world and draw closer to God.  Over these seven days, we will explore what it means to be still before God, surrender our anxieties, wait upon His timing, recognise His voice, and develop a deeper relationship with Him.  The goal is not simply to read seven devotions. It is to develop a lifestyle of stillness, where our hearts remain anchored in God regardless of what happens around us.
